what: CoStar collects data on commercial property: who owns which building, what the rents are, what sold for how much. It sells that to brokers and investors, and it owns Apartments.com, LoopNet and Homes.com.
customers: Commercial property brokers, investors and lenders on subscriptions, and landlords advertising rental listings.
money: commercial listings and the residential portal
moat: A dataset built by researchers who physically verify buildings, which has been compounding for forty years and which no competitor has been willing to fund.
risks: Homes.com has absorbed enormous marketing spending without yet taking meaningful share from Zillow
65 times earnings on a 0.2% net margin, because that spending consumes the profit
Commercial property transaction volumes have been weak, which slows subscription growth
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.9B to $3.2B in four years with $422M of free cash flow
$1.6B of cash against $1.1B of debt, so the Homes.com investment is self-funded
Analysts see about 25% upside, with 20 covering the stock
watch: Net new bookings and whether Homes.com's spending starts producing revenue.
